thread:
incident-bot: Pager alert — Elevated 5xx/error rate from inference-prod in us-west-2a. Observed: DNS resolver latency spikes (~1s+), increased SERVFAILs, and backend i/o timeouts. Potential SLO impact for token success. Runbook: <https://go/runbooks/dns-resolver-impairment>.

alice: I’m on it — seeing increased DNS latencies and a surge of `ECONNRESET` from model worker processes. Are we seeing any ENI or host NIC drops?

dinesh: digging into resolver logs now. Multiple upstream responses with `RCODE=SERVFAIL` and some internal records flipping TTLs wildly (some entries showing TTL=86400 then 30s). Looks like a control-plane push may have introduced bad zone data.

ben: infra view: host network counters look fine, but model workers show repeated `kvcache regen` errors and failing shard fetches: `failed to fetch model shard: dial tcp ... i/o timeout`. Correlation window aligns with first DNS errors.

carla: Can we trigger automatic AZ failover to us-west-2b or a cross-region fallback? If autoswitch didn’t trigger, we might need manual reroute to avoid customer impact.

alice: Plan: (1) pause new traffic to affected nodes in us-west-2a, (2) enable cross-region fallback routing to us-west-2b, (3) drain in-flight requests on the bad host pool. Executing now.

alice: Runbook commands I’m running:
```
# mark region degraded
./infractl set-region-status --region us-west-2a --status degraded --reason "DNS resolver SERVFAIL"
# enable fallback route
./infractl update-routing --policy cross-region-fallback --from us-west-2a --to us-west-2b
```

deploy-bot: Controlplane rollback triggered: rollback of DNS push 4432109200 started by rollback-bot. Status: in-progress.

dinesh: Rollback shows reduced SERVFAILs on upstream, but negative caches are still present on many hosts. We need to flush local resolver caches and lower TTLs temporarily to speed re-propagation.

ben: Temporary mitigation: restart resolver proxy on affected hostpool and clear DNS caches. Pushed an orca job to run this across the fleet (job-id=job-1134). Commands: 
```
sudo systemctl restart redwood-resolver-proxy
sudo /usr/local/bin/clear-dns-cache
```

carla: Customer impact: CS tickets spiked — ~12 active tickets citing timeouts and degraded latency for embeddings and long-context generation. Dashboard shows token success rate dip and higher client retries. I'll escalate to the accounts team for top customers.

eve: Drafting external status update: "We're seeing degraded inference in us-west-2a due to DNS resolver instability. Traffic is being routed to an alternate AZ while we remediate. We'll post updates as we have them." Will post after you confirm routing is applied.

alice: Routing update: cross-region-fallback applied successfully. Metrics: token success rate recovered from ~72% -> ~94% for non-streaming APIs. Streaming tail latency improved but some hung connections still timing out on old sockets.

dinesh: `kvcache regen` events are dropping off. Starting a prewarm job to fetch hot KV shards to avoid cold misses once we allow traffic back: prewarm job id prewarm-887 kicked off.

ben: On-call handoff in 10m. @carla please take incident lead. I'll leave these pinned actions: ensure prewarm completes, keep cross-region routing until TTLs stabilize, validate controlplane rollback fully applied.

carla: Ack — taking lead. My checklist: 1) monitor token success and error rates continuously, 2) keep region status degraded until negative caches expire and we confirm stable DNS answers, 3) confirm CS messages sent and update affected customers. If event window >30m, we'll open a postmortem.

alice: Logged timeline and mitigation steps into incident tracker INC-4432109876. Please append any additional notes.

incident-bot: Pager status: mitigation in progress. Marked as acknowledged by on-call. Please update incident status once all systems stable and traffic is fully returned to us-west-2a.
